title: Translative covering densities of order n log n
main_claim: For all large n there is a centrally symmetric convex body K_n in R^n (a ball of radius ~1+2^-30 cut by Poisson-random symmetric slabs) with translative covering density theta_T(K_n) > c n log n. Rogers' upper bound then gives the sharp order n log n for the worst-case translative covering density.
coverage:
I read every section (2-10) line by line and re-derived the following:
- Volume lemma: E|K| >= e^{-1} w_n a^n, |K| < 3 w_n a^n, and the resulting Markov bound.
- Localization (Sec 3): the three good-point failure probabilities 1/200, 3/2000 and 5/2000, including the exact weighted integral 2n/(n+2); E M(z) <= N_n/40; rounding error delta_n and the Lipschitz factor of w_a; covering by K^+ surviving rounding; the pattern count log|F_n| <= exp(lambda0 n + O(log n)).
- Cap lemma (Sec 4): the Mills-type bounds and hazard bounds for F_n; the bisector identity (1-q^2)/(1-t^2) = 1 - t^2 tan^2(theta/2)/(1-t^2), checked algebraically; the thin-shell fact n(tau-upsilon)^2 -> 0; the tangent sub-Gaussian bound and union bound in the lens estimate; the inequality chain u.e_i >= tau_0; the disjointness corollary (cos 2sqrt(eps) < 1/a).
- Block proposition (Sec 5): the merge and terminality count, the bin parameters (A1, A2, delta), the n^{2 - delta*B0/2} tail, and the large-q_S case.
- Janson (Sec 6): the Harris step, the private-Bernoulli trick with q = m/Delta*, the cell approximation and collision error, and the identification of matching diagrams. In the self-diagram product bound, w_ij = h_ij (delta_i delta_j)^{-1/2}. In the cross bound, the exponent is C n^{2P1+P0 - cH^2} summed over at most n^4 block pairs.
- Targets (Sec 7): the cylinder estimate and the ratio w_{n-1}/w_n <= sqrt(n); the fine-scale exponent -3/8 n log n; 8sqrt(eps)/D = 1/4, so gamma = log 4 - 2 lambda0 > lambda0; the bin-tail algebra giving 1/(8(e^{C*R}/m + 10 n^{-3} Q^2 f_n)); the choice c0 = 1/(64 C*), which gives m e^{-C*R} >= exp(n log n/32).
- Assembly, strict-inequality handling, periodization appendix, rational-polytope corollary and rational-normal proposition.
I did not check external citations (Li-Liu, Prosanov, Rogers) beyond their stated use. The paper reproves the Li-Liu ingredients it needs.

issues.description: The claim that sup theta_L has order n log n relies on the companion paper OpenAI2026SingleLattice (theta_L(K) <= C n log n for all convex bodies). This paper does not verify it, and classical results (Rogers' lattice bound n^{log2 log n + c}) do not supply it. The main Theorem 1.1 and the translative statements do not depend on it.
issues.evidence: Proof of Corollary cor:sharp-order: 'The companion single-lattice theorem [Theorem 1.1, OpenAI2026SingleLattice] gives theta_L(K) <= Cn log n ... which supplies the two lattice upper bounds.'
